title: 3.8.7 Lab: Stringify an Object and Spot What Got Dropped
description: Build an object that has a method and an undefined property, stringify it, and find out in the output what JSON refused to carry. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an object with a method and an undefined value
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it counter; use any name that fits) and assign it an object. Give it a number property, a function property (a method), and a third property whose value is undefined.

steps.title: Stringify it
steps.instructions: Use JSON.stringify on counter and store the result in a second variable.

steps.title: Log the JSON text
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the stringified result. Read it and find which properties survived.

requirements.title: Object declared
requirements.description: Declares an object with curly braces. Help: 3.8.6 (What Does Not Survive)
requirements.hint: Declare an object in braces (the lesson calls it counter) with a number property.

requirements.title: A function value in the object
requirements.description: One property's value is a function. Help: 3.8.6 (What Does Not Survive)
requirements.hint: Give the object a method: a property whose value is a function.

requirements.title: JSON.stringify used
requirements.description: Calls JSON.stringify on the object. Help: 3.8.4 (JSON.stringify — Object to Text)
requirements.hint: Call JSON.stringify on counter and keep the text in a second variable.

requirements.title: Result logged
requirements.description: Calls console.log on the stringified value. Help: 3.8.6 (What Does Not Survive)
requirements.hint: Print the text and read it carefully: look for which properties are missing from it.

requirements.title: counter has a number, a method and an undefined value, and the JSON text is printed
requirements.description: counter holds a number, a function and a property whose value is undefined, and the JSON text was printed. Help: 3.8.6 (What Does Not Survive)
requirements.hint: Give counter a number property, a method (a function value) and a property set to undefined, then print JSON.stringify(counter).

checks.expr: (() => { const LC = (s) => String(s).toLowerCase(); const NUMS = (s) => (String(s).match(/-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:e[-+]?\d+)?/gi) || []).map(Number); const NEAR = (x, y) => typeof x === 'number' && typeof y === 'number' && (x === y || Math.abs(x - y) <= Math.max(0.0051, Math.abs(y) * 1e-9)); const SAMEV = (x, y) => typeof x === 'number' && typeof y === 'number' ? NEAR(x, y) : JSON.stringify(x) === JSON.stringify(y); const SAMEA = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length === b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[i])); const CONTIG = (a, b) => Array.isArray(a) && Array.isArray(b) && a.length > 0 && a.length <= b.length && b.some((_, at) => at + a.length <= b.length && a.every((x, i) => SAMEV(x, b[at + i]))); const JEQ = (a, b) => JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b); const PRINTS = (J, vs) => vs.every((x) => typeof x === 'number' ? NUMS(J).some((y) => NEAR(y, x)) : J.includes(String(x))); const JSONS = (t) => { const found = []; const txt = String(t).slice(0, 20000); for (let i = 0; i < txt.length && found.length < 40; i++) { if (txt[i] !== '{' && txt[i] !== '[') continue; let d = 0; let q = false; for (let j = i; j < txt.length; j++) { const ch = txt[j]; if (q) { if (ch === '\\') j++; else if (ch === '"') q = false; continue; } if (ch === '"') q = true; else if (ch === '{' || ch === '[') d++; else if (ch === '}' || ch === ']') { d--; if (d === 0) { try { found.push(JSON.parse(txt.slice(i, j + 1))); } catch (e) { } break; } } } } return found; }; return (counter !== null && typeof counter === 'object' && Object.values(counter).some(v => typeof v === 'number') && Object.values(counter).some(v => typeof v === 'function') && Object.keys(counter).some(k => counter[k] === undefined) && JSONS(output.join('\n')).some((o) => o !== null && typeof o === 'object' && !Array.isArray(o) && JEQ(o, JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(counter))))); })()
checks.fail: counter needs a number, a method and an undefined property, and you must print the JSON text of counter. That text is shorter than counter: it leaves out the method and the undefined value.

requirements.title: the JSON text printed is made from counter by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints the text JSON.stringify made from counter, and that text changes when counter does. Help: 3.8.6 (What Does Not Survive)
requirements.hint: Keep JSON.stringify(counter) in a variable and print that variable. console.log(counter) prints the object, not the JSON text, and typed-in text does not count.

checks.fail: Print the JSON text made from counter, console.log(json), with a console.log that runs. console.log(counter) prints the object, not the JSON text; typed-in text does not count.
